shared_context.problem:
To make $x$ cakes, a pastry shop uses the following amounts of ingredients:

- $\frac{5x+3}{2}$ packs of chocolate

- $\frac{4x+1}{6}$ packs of butter

- $\frac{13x+5}{20}$ packs of flour

feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that the entire cake corresponds to the full angle of ${360}^{∘}.$

By the angle addition postulate,

$$
m∠A+m∠B+m∠C={360}^{∘}.
$$

Therefore, by substituting the expressions for $m∠A,$ $m∠B,$ and $m∠C,$ and solving for $z,$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠A+m∠B+m∠C & ={360}^{∘} \\ (23z+{4}^{∘})+(12z+{6}^{∘})+(15z) & ={360}^{∘} \\ 50z+{10}^{∘} & ={360}^{∘} \\ 50z & ={350}^{∘} \\ z & ={7}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
